name: Gaussian Partitioning (Count-Then-Fill Binning)
definition: A two-pass CUDA binning algorithm to assign gaussians to macro-tiles, consuming a per-warp visibility bitmask to cull invisible gaussians before intersection tests.
summary: Gaussian Partitioning is a two-pass CUDA binning algorithm that assigns 3D Gaussians to macro-tiles using batch-local atomics and hierarchical prefix scans, eliminating the need for global sorting.
